intro_html: Bright, lemony Greek chicken over tender potatoes is comfort food that doesn't weigh you down. This bowl carries 61 grams of protein for about $4.07 a serving (at everyday cost), and the potato base keeps it hearty and cheap. Fourteen servings out of one pot is a week and a half of no-fuss dinners.
cost_closing_html: About $4.07 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl lands at 61 grams of protein and 555 calories, one of the leaner plates in the bunch.
upsell_html: Fresh, filling, and easy on the wallet. Weeknight dinner doesn't get much friendlier. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Potatoes are one of the cheapest fillers going, so buy the ten-pound bag and let it anchor meals all month.
Olive oil looks expensive by the bottle, but a couple tablespoons here costs pennies, so one good bottle stretches for months.
Bottled lime juice works fine and never spoils, so keep it in the fridge door instead of buying fresh citrus you'll forget about.
make_it: Add the chicken, olive oil, lime juice, red wine vinegar, and garlic to the slow cooker and toss to coat.
Nestle the cut potatoes around and under the chicken so they cook in the juices.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the potatoes are fork-tender and the chicken shreds.
Shred the chicken and stir everything together so the potatoes catch the tangy sauce.
Serve the chicken and potatoes together, spooning the pan juices over the top.
